questions.q: What does CREATE do when you run the same CREATE statement twice in Cypher?
options: It inserts two separate nodes, since CREATE never checks whether an equivalent node already exists
It creates the node the first time and silently does nothing the second time
It throws a duplicate key error, just like a SQL Server unique constraint violation
It automatically merges the two into one node
questions.explain: CREATE is an unconditional insert with no built-in duplicate check — running it twice produces two separate nodes unless a unique constraint is defined.

questions.q: How does MERGE decide whether to create a new node or match an existing one?
options: It searches for a node matching the entire specified pattern (labels and properties); if found it binds to it like MATCH, if not found it creates it like CREATE
It always creates a new node regardless of what already exists
It only checks a node's internal ID, ignoring labels and properties
It requires a separate unique constraint before it can run at all
questions.explain: MERGE matches on the whole pattern you specify — different properties in the pattern mean a different match target, and possibly a new node.

questions.q: What is the purpose of ON CREATE SET and ON MATCH SET on a MERGE clause?
options: They run different property updates depending on whether MERGE created a new node or matched an existing one
They are required before any MERGE statement will execute
They delete the node if the condition isn't met
They convert MERGE into a plain CREATE statement
questions.explain: ON CREATE SET fires only on the create branch, ON MATCH SET only on the match branch, letting one MERGE statement handle both cases differently.

questions.q: Why does Neo4j refuse to run DELETE on a node that still has relationships attached to it?
options: To avoid leaving a dangling relationship pointing at a deleted node
Because DELETE only works on relationships, never on nodes
Because deleting a connected node would violate Cypher's syntax rules
Neo4j does not actually have this restriction
questions.explain: A relationship is a stored object pointing to two nodes — deleting one endpoint without handling the relationship would leave a broken pointer, so Neo4j blocks the plain DELETE.

questions.q: What does DETACH DELETE do that a plain DELETE cannot?
options: It removes a node along with every relationship attached to it, in a single statement
It deletes an entire label from the database
It performs a soft delete that can be undone later
It only works on relationships, not nodes
questions.explain: DETACH DELETE is the practical default for fully removing a node — it deletes the node and all its attached relationships together, similar to a cascading delete.
